A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SITE benchmark. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material are readable and can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM evaluations, human-study outcomes, and LIBERO-Spatial manipulation experiments in Tables 3–6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original model, human, and robot-manipulation results, including the supplementary correlation analysis.

M1.justification: The filtering, categorization, stratified sampling, view-association, and frame-reordering procedures remain the same. Removing 'two-stage' and 'second' wording in Section 4.1 does not remove the described operations; Figure 2 and the supplementary prompts retain the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 22 image datasets, eight video datasets, Ego-Exo4D tasks, and LIBERO-Spatial evaluation. The final benchmark remains 8,068 questions. Changing '31 datasets' to '30 existing datasets' plus the newly annotated source clarifies accounting rather than changing coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 3–4 retain the same nine VLM configurations and human/random references. Tables 5–6 retain the same four LLaVA-OneVision/Qwen2.5-VL configurations, and Table 6 retains the same comparison benchmarks.

E3.justification: Validation/test sourcing, CAA scoring, GPT-4o judging, human-study sampling, and LIBERO-Spatial training settings are unchanged. The introduction's revised bottom-up question counts reconcile it with existing Table 2 rather than establish a changed experimental sample or protocol.

E4.justification: New Figure 12 analyzes which source datasets contribute to each of the six spatial categories, extending v1's aggregate category distributions. It exposes source concentration, including Ego-Exo4D's dominance in multi-view questions. Existing supplementary examples and correlation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The averaging over human participants, plus/minus reporting in Tables 5–6, and Pearson-correlation reporting are unchanged. No additional repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures appear.

E6.justification: The introduction corrects the correlation from 0.922 to 0.902, already reported in Tables 5–6, and bottom-up question counts from 8,068 to 6,943, consistent with Table 2. Figure 12 adds source-level composition results. All numerical entries in Tables 2–6 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 1 defining chance-adjusted accuracy and its stated properties are unchanged. Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs, and the spatial-category definitions remain substantively identical.

C1.justification: Both versions claim comprehensive spatial-intelligence evaluation, three cognitive classification systems, two perspective-related tasks, a substantial human–model gap, and positive association with manipulation performance. The numerical corrections do not change these contributions' meaning or scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 removes the paragraph hypothesizing that humans succeed through lived experience while VLMs rely on pixel-level similarities rather than geometric understanding and temporal dynamics. Other explanations involving training-data coverage, model scale, and grounding remain.

D1.justification: v2 removes the abstract's explicit promise that code and data will become publicly available, while retaining the same project-page link. This changes the access-related disclosure without establishing any actual availability change. Implementation settings and supplementary prompt details remain substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Kim et al. on spatial reasoning in human IQ tests and Marsili et al. on visual agentic spatial reasoning. It replaces the general Qwen2.5 report with the Qwen2.5-VL report and drops MM-Vet v2. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes local grammar, terminology, attribution, and bibliographic corrections, tightens several passages, and removes one explanatory paragraph. The main section sequence and supplementary organization remain intact rather than undergoing extensive restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 adds the six-panel dataset-composition chart as Figure 12 and relocates Table 3 from the right to the left column. Text and references reflow, but existing figure artwork and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves internal consistency by distinguishing reused from newly annotated questions and correcting the introduction's correlation to match Tables 5–6. Figure 12 also improves transparency about dataset composition. These are limited gains with unchanged experimental evidence; removing the explicit code/data release promise reduces access-related clarity, although the project link remains.
